source.title: ACMo: Angle-Calibrated Moment Methods for Stochastic Optimization
source.authors: Xun-Peng Huang; Run-Xin Xu; Hao Zhou; Zhe Wang; Zheng-Yang Liu; Lei Li

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and supplementary proofs; some equations and figure labels are garbled, but the relevant optimizer comparisons are described in text.
record.tranche_reason: It compares a newly proposed optimizer with standard optimizers and reports training-loss and held-out performance on natural image and translation tasks, bearing on V4. The optimizer comparison is not a direct reproduction of the cited adaptive-optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: Reports optimizer performance and test accuracy on natural-label tasks. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus fully connected architectures, batch-size effects, dropout, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples. Figure-only learning curves lack exact numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study reports held-out comparisons between established adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD on image classification and translation. These bear on V4 independently of the proposed ACMo optimizer. Image experiments tune momentum and adaptive-method parameters as well as learning rates, and sometimes weight decay, so they do not reproduce the limited-tuning protocol exactly.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose ACMo as a first-moment optimizer with a nonconvex gradient-norm convergence rate comparable to Adam-type methods, and report competitive empirical convergence with better held-out performance in most comparisons. SGD-momentum remains best in their fixed-weight-decay image experiments, while ACMo is comparable to Adam and AdamW and better than SGD-momentum in fixed-learning-rate translation.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates ACMo, a new first-moment optimizer; compares its results with existing optimizers on image classification and machine translation rather than reproducing the cited optimizer studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences by dataset/task, architecture, weight-decay selection (fixed versus individually optimal), and fixed-learning-rate translation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: ACMo's convergence theorem, reduced second-moment storage, and standalone performance ranking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A first-moment optimizer can achieve convergence and held-out performance competitive with Adam-type methods.

record.problems: Optimizer comparisons on image classification use plotted learning curves without exact reported scores in the text. No uncertainty estimates are stated. For NMT, the paper uses a fixed step size and gradient clipping to remove learning tricks, limiting what it establishes about broader tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible optimizer-result rows were omitted. The paper presents per-architecture learning curves in Figures 2 and 3, but the supplied text gives only aggregate qualitative descriptions and no recoverable per-architecture values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.

A protocol tuning only learning rates and schedules; a controlled test that broader tuning removes an initial disadvantage; recovery by decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers; word-level language modeling. AdamW is included, but the prose does not establish recovery relative to Adam.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to large-batch training recipes.
Dropout and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and rankings of generalization-gap measures.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure text does not preserve identifiable curve values, so exact scores and additional architecture-specific rankings cannot be reconstructed. Fixed versus individually optimized weight decay is also confounded with CIFAR-100 versus CIFAR-10; these experiments do not isolate the effect of tuning. R1 and R2 duplicate the same ranking and should not count as independent evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language-model comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive large-batch recipes.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: SGD-momentum
rows.operation_detail: Compared CIFAR-100 test accuracy with optimizers using fixed weight decay selected from the SGD-momentum maximum-test-accuracy setting.

conditions.value: fixed at the SGD-momentum setting yielding maximum test accuracy

rows.measure: test accuracy; training loss convergence described qualitatively
rows.value: The paper says ACMo was second only to SGD-momentum in generalization performance; no exact value stated.
rows.locator: Section 5.1, Experiment with Fixed Weight Decay; Figure 2
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison across the three architectures; exact scores are only plotted.
rows.check: The qualitative ranking supports the adaptive-optimizer disadvantage: SGD-momentum ranks above ACMo, which ranks above the adaptive benchmarks. Replace partial with observed. The shared weight decay was selected for SGD, and optimizer hyperparameters beyond learning rates were tuned.

rows.subject: ACMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy and training-loss convergence with optimizers using fixed weight decay.

conditions.value: fixed at the SGD-momentum setting yielding maximum test accuracy

rows.baseline: Other tested optimizers; paper states ACMo outperformed all benchmarks except SGD-momentum in test accuracy.
rows.value: ACMo was second only to SGD-momentum in generalization performance and significantly faster than SGD-momentum, Adam, and AMSGrad in convergence speed; comparable in speed to SOTA Adam variants.
rows.locator: Section 5.1, Experiment with Fixed Weight Decay; Figure 2
rows.note: Qualitative summary for three CNN architectures; exact scores are only plotted.
rows.check: The reported ranking implies that the established adaptive benchmarks generalize worse than SGD-momentum, duplicating R1. ACMo is a proposed first-moment method; its own performance and convergence speed alone do not establish V4. Separate training convergence from held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: ACMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimal-weight-decay test accuracy and efficiency with other optimizers.

conditions.value: optimal value chosen for each optimizer to achieve best test accuracy

rows.baseline: Other tested optimizers, including SGD-momentum, Adam, AdamW, AMSGrad, PAdam, and Adabound
rows.value: ACMo obtained top three generalization results across architectures; on VGGNet, ACMo, PAdam, and Adabound could outperform SGD-momentum, while these methods outperformed Adam by more than 2 percentage points in test accuracy.
rows.locator: Section 5.1, Experiment with Optimal Weight Decay; Figure 3
rows.note: The paper reports the comparisons qualitatively; exact values are only plotted. Its claim that faster-converging optimizers generalize worse is also qualitative.
rows.check: This aggregate mixes optimizer rankings and architectures. Split the VGGNet result where PAdam and Adabound beat SGD-momentum from the poorer Adam-family results. The greater-than-two-percentage-point comparison is against Adam, not SGD. Individually selected weight decay and additional optimizer-parameter tuning are material conditions.

rows.subject: ACMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared development loss and BLEU with other optimizers at fixed step size and gradient clipping.
rows.baseline: Adam and AdamW are the stated performance reference; SGD-momentum and other adaptive methods also compared.
rows.value: ACMo yielded development-loss and BLEU results comparable with Adam and AdamW, and better results than SGD-momentum; it outperformed Adabound and PAdam after rapid middle-stage descent.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; exact values are only plotted. Results described for a fixed-learning-rate setting.
rows.check: The relevant result is the adaptive-method advantage over SGD-momentum in fixed-learning-rate translation, explicitly described in Section 5.2. ACMo itself is a first-moment method. Replace partial with reversed for the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison and distinguish development loss from BLEU.
